text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: Sega Model 3 was an arcade hardware platform released in 1996 as the successor to Sega Model 2. It featured a much more powerful PowerPC-based architecture and advanced Real3D graphics technology developed with Lockheed Martin. Model 3 delivered some of the most impressive arcade visuals of the late 1990s, powering games such as Virtua Fighter 3, Sega Rally 2, Scud Race, Star Wars Trilogy Arcade, and The Lost World: Jurassic Park. Its advanced 3D graphics helped bridge the gap between traditional arcade machines and the emerging home console generation.
